text:
jen: noticing a spike of CUDA OOMs on us-west1-gpu-*/runtime pods starting ~08:02 UTC. headroom shows ~10-14GB free on nodes though. :thinking:

miguel: looking. are these new model variants or increased batch size?

jen: no recent rollout, traffic uptick from a single customer ramp. sequence lengths normal. KV-cache eviction rate jumped.

maya: adding telemetry: allocator reports lots of small reserved blocks pinned, fragmentation high. suspect reserve pinning by prefetch.

leo: paste of the top allocator logs:
```
[08:02:10] reserve: alloc 2.5GB reserved_block id=0x7f9e pinned=true owner=kvcache
[08:02:11] fragment: free_chunks=18 total_free=11GB largest_free=1.2GB
[08:02:12] cudaOOM: request 3.2GB cannot satisfy despite headroom=12GB
```

jen: so headroom metric is global free memory but fragmentation prevents contiguous allocation.

sam: oncall-bot escalation: @infra oncall, please triage - customer requests degraded perf, some requests failing with 500 and "cuda runtime error: out of memory". :rotating_light:

oncall-bot: PagerDuty alert created PD#8471. Current severity: S2 (customer impact: degraded inference for a subset of shards).

miguel: quick mitigation options: 1) trigger soft-evict of kvcache for affected model shards, 2) increase reserve-size to reduce fragmentation pressure, 3) restart runtime pods (fast but causes in-flight failures), 4) node drain + recreate on larger instance. prefer non-disruptive first.

maya: soft-evict worked historically for small bursts. command:
```bash
redwoodctl runtime evict-kvcache --selector model=rw-13b --pct=60 --reason "oom-frag emergency"
```

leo: I'm going to run evict-kvcache for the two offending nodes now. will monitor memory maps and OOMs.

jen: +1 do it. notify customers if we expect >1min impact.

infra-bot: action: evict-kvcache job queued -> job-3337 status=running.

(30s later)

leo: evict job completed on node us-west1-gpu-12/13. KV cache dropped ~45% on affected shards. fragmentation metric drop ~18%. OOMs still appear but much reduced.

miguel: ok positive signal. next: schedule rolling restart for remaining high-frag pods with graceful drain to let in-flight RPCs finish: command:
```bash
kubectl rollout restart deploy/rl-runtime --namespace=prod -l az=us-west1-gpu -n prod --grace-period=60
```

maya: note: restarting will flush KV cache, causing extra token compute and some latency for warmups. recommend informing customer ops.

jen: customer-ops pinged: "we see some failures, thanks for triage. please estimate recovery time." Maya: ETA 6-8m for restarts + warmup.

sam: also enabling an automatic fallback route to model-variant cpu-safe to reduce customer error rate while we restore: featureflag toggle id=ff-fallback-312 set=on.

infra-bot: action: featureflag ff-fallback-312 toggled by sam at 08:10 UTC.

(rollout progresses)

leo: restarts done for az us-west1-gpu, nodes stabilized, no new OOMs for 5m. latency spike observed during warmup ~+220ms p95 for ~3m.

miguel: root cause analysis notes so far: prefetch + aggressive reserve allocation caused many small pinned reserved blocks; combined with long-running KV cache entries reduced coalescing opportunities leading to contiguous allocation failures. headroom metric misleading because it doesn't reflect fragmentation.

maya: short term mitigation doc: 1) soft-evict kvcache on affected shards 2) prefer cache-pressure-based proactive evictions on ramping traffic 3) add fragmentation-aware headroom metric (largest contiguous chunk) 4) consider reserve defragmentation via periodic slab compaction.

jen: filing follow-up tasks: ENG-RUNTIME-1426 (fragmentation metric), ENG-RUNTIME-1427 (proactive kv eviction policy), ENG-OPS-923 (runbook updates).

sam: customer impact summary for PD ticket: ~S2, affected ~1% of qps for 12m window, errors 500->reduced to baseline after mitigations, latency bump during warmup. sent to customer success.

leo: tagging logs for postmortem: add label oom-frag-hidden-2026 and capture memory maps from nodes us-west1-gpu-12/13.

oncall-bot: Incident thread closed for active mitigation. please update postmortem when available. :white_check_mark:
